description: We are building a row of four two-storey townhouses in Calgary, each with a legal basement secondary suite. The building area is 400 m2. Stick-framed lumber rafters and ceiling joists from the Part 9 span tables (no roof trusses); floor joists span 4.4 m; plain concrete footings and foundation walls from the Section 9.15 tables; no sprinkler or fire alarm system; not on permafrost; the building official has not asked for professional drawings. The longest rafter is a 4.1 m clear span.
known_facts: each townhouse has a basement secondary suite

gold.engineering_reason: Code exception passes: 4 principal units, suites need not count (Div C 2.4.1.1.(1)(b)(ii) and (2)). Counting suites as dwelling units gives 8, above the Acts' "4 dwelling units or less" (Architects Act s.2(6)(b)(ii); EGPA s.2(7)(b)(ii)). A registered architect (authorized entity) is required for the design (Architects Act s.2(1)).
gold.limit_source: Architects Act s.2(1), s.2(6)(b)(ii); EGPA s.2(7)(b)(ii); Div C 2.4.1.1.(2); Div A 1.4.1.2.(1).

authoring.label: model-constructed, model-checked, not human-verified
authoring.notes: Constructed scenario, not a real case. Gold written from the quoted sources before any system run. Not human-reviewed. Code-vs-Act suite counting divergence; code exception sits exactly at its 4-unit limit.
